lenses.sp: Wants a large, steady, cheap company with a strong balance sheet.

ch.r: Market value above ₹5,000 crore

ch.r: Current assets ÷ current liabilities ≥ 2

ch.r: Long-term debt ≤ current assets − current liabilities
ch.v: Long-term debt ₹665 cr vs working capital ₹1,904 cr
ch.w: Graham wanted the short-term cushion alone to be able to repay long-term loans.

ch.n: A profit every year for 10 years

ch.v: Profit in all 4 yrs we have
ch.w: No loss in the years we can see; the earlier years are not in the free data.

ch.r: Dividends every year for 20 years (India: 10 years)
ch.w: 10 dividends in 10 years with no gap longer than 18 months.

ch.n: Earnings per share up a third in 10 years
ch.r: EPS +33% over 10 years (3-year averages at each end)
ch.w: EPS (average of the first 2 vs last 2 years we have) moved +54%.

ch.r: PE ≤ 15 on 3-year average earnings
ch.w: You pay ₹43 for every ₹1 of average yearly profit over the last 3 yrs.
You pay ₹5.22 for every ₹1 of net worth.

ch.r: Price < √(22.5 × EPS × book value per share)
ch.w: With EPS ₹69.0 and book value ₹487 per share, Graham's ceiling price is ₹869.

story.what_it_does: Endurance Technologies is an auto parts maker. It makes items such as brake systems, ABS, suspension parts, alloy wheels and battery packs, selling in India and Europe. Consolidated income was about ₹14,720 crore in FY26.
story.plans: Management plans India capex of about ₹800 crore in FY27, with new plants for battery packs, ABS and brake expansion, aluminium forging and alloy wheels. It also plans to take the Stöferle stake to 100% (done per the Sep-26 release), add Fondalpress in Italy, and cut the ICE share of Europe revenue to 25% by FY28.
story.moat: The notes point to a strong brake position, with a 34.5% brake systems market share and 14.3% scooter market share, plus 96 patents. Order wins such as ₹1,596 crore in India in FY26 and EV-related wins suggest customer relationships that support growth. The notes do not describe a formal moat beyond this.

scenarios.story: New plants for ABS, battery packs, alloy wheels and forging ramp up while cost pass-through and softer aluminium prices lift margins. Order wins keep feeding sales growth that has already run at 30% or more.
signals_to_watch: Consolidated EBITDA margin recovering from 12.1% in Q2 FY27
Bidkin alloy wheel utilisation rising from 60% toward full use by end of FY27

scenarios.story: Sales keep growing strongly in India, but margins stay below last year's 14%-plus levels while raw material costs are passed on with a lag. Europe stays weak as ICE revenue declines and Stöferle and Fondalpress add some support.
signals_to_watch: Whether cost pass-through to OEMs is completed
Europe revenue growth beyond the 1% in euro terms seen in Q1 FY27

scenarios.story: Raw material, energy and freight costs stay high and pass-through lags, so profit keeps growing slower than sales. Europe's ICE-to-EV shift, Chinese OEM competition and local-content rules hurt the European business further.
signals_to_watch: Further falls in consolidated EBITDA margin, which was 12.1% in Q2 FY27
Europe profit hit by accelerated depreciation of phased-out OEM programme assets
